name: Reptile Meta-RL
analogy: Think of it as a coach who sends a trainee to practise on one market for a week, then moves the trainee's default stance a little toward wherever the practice ended up. After many markets, the default stance sits in a place from which any new market is a short walk away.

steps.title: Pick a task and copy the shared weights
steps.description: A task is a stretch of market history, such as a block of bars. The shared starting weights are copied so that practice on the task never damages the shared original.
steps.inExample: The task is one block of 500 five-minute MNQ bars, and a copy of the shared policy is made.

steps.title: Practise on the task with ordinary training
steps.description: The copy is trained with plain gradient steps on that task's data for a handful of steps. No special support and query split is needed, and nothing fancy is differentiated.
steps.inExample: Five steps with an inner learning rate of 5 hundredths move one example weight from 400 thousandths to 520 thousandths.

steps.title: Measure how far practice moved the weights
steps.description: The difference between the practised weights and the shared starting weights is taken. That difference points toward weights that work well on this task.
steps.inExample: For the example weight the difference is plus 120 thousandths.

steps.title: Move the shared start a small step toward it
steps.description: The shared weights are nudged a fraction of the way along that difference. Averaging this over a few tasks at a time smooths out the noise.
steps.inExample: With an outer step size of 10 percent the shared weight moves by 12 thousandths, from 400 to 412 thousandths.

steps.title: Repeat across many tasks
steps.description: The cycle repeats over many blocks and instruments, shrinking the outer step slowly. The shared weights drift toward a place that is close to good solutions for many tasks at once.
steps.inExample: After thousands of blocks the shared starting point sits within a few steps of a good policy for most MNQ and ES blocks.

steps.title: Fine-tune on the new task
steps.description: At deployment the shared weights are fine-tuned for a few ordinary steps on the earlier known bars just before a new block, and that tuned copy then chooses positions.
steps.inExample: The tuned policy gives 38 percent long, 34 percent flat and 28 percent short for the newest bar.

useFor.task: A cheap shared start for fine-tuning to a new instrument
useFor.example: Producing starting weights that adapt to a newly added contract in a few steps, without any advanced meta-learning code.

useFor.task: Frequent refreshes of a shared model
useFor.example: Keeping the shared start current every week as new 5-minute bars arrive, with only ordinary training code.

useFor.task: Short fine-tuning after a regime change
useFor.example: Adapting to a newly flagged high-volatility regime using five steps on the preceding bars.
Testing whether any shared start helps before investing in a heavier method.

avoidWhen: Adaptation must happen from only one or two gradient steps; a method that optimises the first step directly is a better fit.
Your tasks are almost identical blocks of one steady market; ordinary training on all the data does the same job with less machinery.

example.scenario: A shared policy has been built by cycling over many MNQ blocks. A new block begins, and the policy is fine-tuned on the 150 earlier bars whose outcomes are already known, then asked about the newest bar.

input.summary: The shared weights, the inner practice settings and the earlier bars for fine-tuning.

fields.name: example shared weight
fields.meaning: One number inside the shared starting policy, followed through the example.

fields.name: inner steps
fields.meaning: How many ordinary training steps are taken on the task.

fields.name: inner learning rate
fields.meaning: How large each practice step is.

fields.name: outer step size
fields.meaning: What fraction of the way the shared weights move toward the practised ones.

fields.name: fine-tuning bars
fields.meaning: The earlier bars with known outcomes used to tune the copy before the new block.

fields.name: average true range, 14 bars
fields.meaning: The typical high-to-low travel of a recent bar.

output.summary: An updated shared weight from training, and the tuned policy's preference for the newest bar.

fields.name: example shared weight after the outer step
fields.meaning: The shared weight after moving one tenth of the way toward the practised value of 520 thousandths.

fields.name: share long
fields.meaning: The tuned policy's preference for a long position.

fields.name: share flat
fields.meaning: The tuned policy's preference for staying out.

fields.name: share short
fields.meaning: The tuned policy's preference for a short position.

fields.name: probability the close is higher
fields.meaning: The long share divided by the long and short shares combined.

example.reading: The shared weight changes slowly by design; judge the method by how much the tuned copy earns beyond the same shared start with no fine-tuning steps. The 58 percent lean is only a direction call and has to clear trading costs on later bars.
